name: Aloe Vera
light: Bright light with several hours of sun; acclimate gradually before placing it in stronger direct sun.
pot_note: Use a pot with multiple drainage holes; an unglazed clay pot can help the mix dry. Do not let the pot stand in drained water.

watering.rule: Let the potting mix dry out completely, then water thoroughly and let excess water drain away. Reduce watering during cool, low-growth periods.

by_season.summer: Check the mix periodically because heat can speed drying, but water only after it has dried completely.
by_season.monsoon: Shelter the pot from prolonged rain; check that the mix is completely dry before watering.
by_season.autumn: Allow the mix to dry completely between waterings and reassess after each watering.
by_season.winter: Water sparingly and only when the mix is fully dry; cool conditions usually mean slower drying.

watering.avoid: Do not keep the mix continuously wet or leave water in the saucer; persistent moisture can cause root problems.

common_mistakes: Watering before the mix has dried completely
Using a pot without drainage holes
Moving the plant suddenly into intense direct sun

name: Money Plant (Pothos)
light: Medium to bright filtered or indirect light is suitable. Protect it from strong direct sun, which can scorch leaves.
pot_note: Choose a pot with drainage holes and an airy growing medium. A support pole or hanging pot can accommodate its climbing or trailing growth.

watering.rule: Let the soil surface dry slightly before watering. Water thoroughly, then empty the saucer so roots do not sit in water.

by_season.summer: Check the top layer more often in hot or bright conditions; water when the surface has dried slightly.
by_season.monsoon: Check the soil before watering because humid weather and rain can slow drying; never leave the pot standing in water.
by_season.autumn: Water when the surface has dried slightly, adjusting to light and room conditions.
by_season.winter: Check before watering and allow more time for the soil to dry if growth and evaporation slow.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogged soil, prolonged harsh direct sun, and cold drafts.

common_mistakes: Watering while the soil is still wet
Placing it in strong direct afternoon sun
Leaving it in cold drafts

name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
light: Prefer a sunny outdoor position with around six or more hours of direct sun when practical.
pot_note: Use a container with drainage holes and a well-drained, moisture-retentive mix. A sunny balcony or outdoor position is generally better than a dim indoor corner.

watering.rule: Keep the soil lightly and evenly moist while allowing excess water to drain. For established plants, decide from rainfall and soil moisture rather than following a rigid schedule.

by_season.summer: Check the soil frequently in heat; water when the upper layer begins to dry, without allowing the pot to remain waterlogged.
by_season.monsoon: Check soil moisture and recent rainfall before watering; ensure the pot drains freely.
by_season.autumn: Water according to soil moisture and plant growth; do not follow a fixed weekly schedule if the soil is still moist.
by_season.winter: Check before watering and avoid soggy soil, especially when growth slows or nights are cool.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogged soil and watering automatically when rain or still-moist soil has already supplied enough moisture.

common_mistakes: Growing it in insufficient light
Allowing the pot to remain waterlogged
Watering on a fixed schedule without checking rainfall or soil moisture

name: Snake Plant
light: Tolerates low light, but a bright position with indirect light or part-day sun is also suitable. Avoid suddenly exposing indoor leaves to intense sun.
pot_note: Use a sturdy pot with drainage holes and a fast-draining mix. A heavy pot can help support tall leaves.

watering.rule: Allow the mix to dry between waterings. Water thoroughly only when it is dry, then drain away excess water.

by_season.summer: Check the mix before watering; even in warm weather, water only once it has dried out.
by_season.monsoon: Keep the pot sheltered from prolonged rain and wait until the mix is dry before watering.
by_season.autumn: Allow the mix to dry fully between waterings as growth and evaporation change.
by_season.winter: Water much less often; ensure the mix is dry before watering again.

watering.avoid: Avoid frequent watering and persistently wet soil; overwatering can cause root rot.

common_mistakes: Watering too often
Using a pot without drainage
Leaving the root zone persistently wet

name: Spider Plant
light: Medium, indirect light is ideal; it tolerates shade but avoid strong direct sunlight on the leaves.
pot_note: Works well in a pot or hanging basket with drainage holes. Allow room for arching leaves and trailing plantlets.

watering.rule: Aim for lightly moist soil while allowing the surface to dry somewhat between waterings. Reduce watering during winter.

by_season.summer: Check the surface regularly and water when it begins to dry, especially in a warm bright position.
by_season.monsoon: Check the soil first and empty the saucer; humid conditions may mean less frequent watering.
by_season.autumn: Water when the surface begins to dry and the pot feels lighter, rather than by calendar alone.
by_season.winter: Allow longer between waterings as growth and drying slow; avoid keeping the mix saturated.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogging, direct harsh sun, and over-fertilizing. If leaf tips repeatedly brown, consider whether water quality or salt buildup may be contributing.

common_mistakes: Keeping the soil constantly saturated
Exposing leaves to harsh direct sun
Over-fertilizing

name: ZZ Plant
light: Tolerates low light but generally grows best in bright indirect light. Protect it from direct sun that can scorch leaves.
pot_note: Use a pot with drainage holes and a well-drained mix. The thick underground rhizomes store water, so avoid an oversized pot that stays wet for too long.

watering.rule: Allow the potting mix to dry out between waterings. Water thoroughly only when dry and drain excess water.

by_season.summer: Check that the mix is completely dry before watering; do not water just because the weather is hot.
by_season.monsoon: Shelter the pot from prolonged rain and wait for the mix to dry before watering.
by_season.autumn: Water only after the mix dries out; reassess as the plant's growth slows.
by_season.winter: Water sparingly and only after the mix has dried completely.

watering.avoid: Avoid wet feet and frequent watering; waterlogged mix can damage roots and rhizomes.

common_mistakes: Watering while the mix is still wet
Placing it in direct sun
Using a container without drainage

name: Jade Plant
light: Provide bright light and some sun; indoors, use the brightest suitable window and acclimate gradually to stronger sun.
pot_note: Use a pot with drainage holes and a succulent-appropriate, fast-draining mix. Avoid a pot that stays wet for long periods.

watering.rule: Water moderately only after the soil has dried. Reduce watering from autumn through late winter when growth is slower.

by_season.summer: Check the soil and water only after it dries; bright light may increase water use, but do not keep the mix wet.
by_season.monsoon: Keep the pot sheltered from repeated rain and wait until the mix is dry before watering.
by_season.autumn: Begin reducing watering as growth slows; check dryness before each watering.
by_season.winter: Water sparingly, only after the soil has dried well.

watering.avoid: Avoid overwatering and poorly drained soil; excess moisture can lead to leaf drop and root rot.

common_mistakes: Overwatering
Keeping the plant in insufficient light for long periods
Using heavy soil that remains wet

name: Areca Palm
light: Bright indirect light in an indoor setting. Avoid very dark positions and harsh afternoon sun through glass.
pot_note: Use a well-drained potting mix in a container with drainage holes. It appreciates warmth and higher humidity; repot when roots require it rather than excessively often.

watering.rule: During active growth, keep the mix moist but not soggy. Water thoroughly and let excess water drain away.

by_season.summer: Check moisture frequently in hot, bright conditions and water when the mix begins to dry, without waterlogging it.
by_season.monsoon: Check before watering; humidity and rain can slow drying. Keep the pot draining freely.
by_season.autumn: Adjust watering to growth and soil moisture; do not let the mix remain saturated.
by_season.winter: Water less often if growth and drying slow, but do not let the root ball remain bone-dry for long periods.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogged soil, dry air for extended periods, and cold drafts.

common_mistakes: Letting the pot sit in standing water
Placing it in a very dark area
Allowing prolonged cold or very dry indoor conditions

name: Peace Lily
light: Partial to deep shade or bright indirect light; keep it out of direct sun.
pot_note: Use an organic-rich potting mix and a pot with drainage holes. It can tolerate being somewhat pot-bound; repot when it outgrows its container.

watering.rule: Keep the soil moist but not soggy and allow some drying between waterings. Empty the saucer after watering.

by_season.summer: Check moisture more often in warm conditions; water as the mix begins to dry, keeping it evenly moist rather than soaked.
by_season.monsoon: Check the soil before watering and ensure excess water drains; humid conditions can slow drying.
by_season.autumn: Water according to soil moisture and light, not a fixed weekly schedule.
by_season.winter: Allow more time between waterings if growth slows, while preventing the root ball from staying dry for too long.

watering.avoid: Avoid direct sun, waterlogged soil, over-fertilizing, and salt buildup in the potting mix.

common_mistakes: Placing it in direct sunlight
Keeping the soil soggy
Over-fertilizing or allowing salts to build up

name: Rose
light: Choose a sunny position with around six or more hours of direct sunlight where the local climate permits.
pot_note: Use a large, stable container with drainage holes and an organic-rich but well-drained mix. Leave room for root growth and airflow around foliage.

watering.rule: Keep the root zone evenly moist but not waterlogged. Water at the soil surface near the base rather than routinely wetting the foliage.

by_season.summer: Check soil moisture frequently in hot weather; water deeply when needed and allow excess to drain.
by_season.monsoon: Avoid additional watering when rain has already moistened the root zone; ensure free drainage and avoid routinely wetting leaves.
by_season.autumn: Water when the root-zone soil begins to dry, adjusting for temperature and growth.
by_season.winter: Water less often when growth and evaporation slow, but do not let container roots dry out for extended periods.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogging and repeated overhead irrigation that keeps foliage wet; ensure the pot drains freely.

common_mistakes: Insufficient direct light
Poor drainage
Repeatedly wetting foliage when watering

name: Hibiscus
light: Full sun to partial shade, with bright light for container plants. Protect it from strong wind and cold conditions.
pot_note: Use a roomy container with drainage holes and a rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained mix. Avoid frequent moves after buds form because environmental changes can trigger bud or leaf drop.

watering.rule: Keep the root ball moist during active growth, while allowing excess water to drain and avoiding stagnant wet soil.

by_season.summer: Check the pot frequently in hot weather and water when the mix begins to dry; do not let the root ball dry out completely for long.
by_season.monsoon: Check the mix before watering, and confirm that the container drains quickly after rain.
by_season.autumn: Adjust watering as temperatures and growth change; maintain moisture without leaving the pot soggy.
by_season.winter: Water according to soil moisture and growth; protect the plant from cold and avoid keeping the mix continuously wet.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogged roots, drought stress during active growth, frost, and repeated sudden changes in location.

common_mistakes: Letting the root ball dry for too long during active growth
Using a pot with poor drainage
Moving the plant repeatedly during budding or flowering

name: Marigold (African Marigold)
light: Full sun is preferred for flowering. Use a position that receives several hours of direct sunlight.
pot_note: Use a container with drainage holes and a well-drained loamy mix. Avoid water stagnation, particularly after heavy rain.

watering.rule: Water after checking soil moisture; keep the mix reasonably moist during active growth but never stagnant or saturated.

by_season.summer: Check the container regularly in heat and water when the upper soil begins to dry.
by_season.monsoon: Check the mix and recent rainfall before watering; prevent water stagnation around roots.
by_season.autumn: Water when the upper soil begins to dry, adjusting to flowering, warmth, and rainfall.
by_season.winter: Water according to soil moisture; avoid frequent watering if the pot remains damp in cooler weather.

watering.avoid: Avoid water stagnation and allowing the mix to remain saturated after rain.

common_mistakes: Growing in deep shade
Allowing standing water around roots
Watering on a fixed schedule without checking soil moisture

name: Curry Leaf Plant
light: Give it a sunny outdoor position; bright light supports healthy growth.
pot_note: Use a deep container with drainage holes and a well-drained mix. Avoid dense, waterlogged soil.

watering.rule: Water after planting and keep the root zone appropriately moist while it establishes. For established plants, use soil moisture and rainfall to guide watering; field guidance gives weekly irrigation as a general reference, not a universal pot schedule.

by_season.summer: Check soil more often in hot weather and water when needed; containers can dry faster than field soil.
by_season.monsoon: Reduce or skip watering when rainfall has moistened the root zone; ensure drainage is unobstructed.
by_season.autumn: Water according to soil moisture and plant growth rather than a fixed timetable.
by_season.winter: Check before watering and allow more time between waterings if growth and evaporation slow.

watering.avoid: Avoid stagnant water and dense soil that drains poorly.

common_mistakes: Using poorly drained soil
Watering routinely despite wet soil or rainfall
Keeping the plant in a low-light indoor location long term

name: Lucky Bamboo
light: Bright indirect light or partial shade; keep it out of harsh direct sunlight.
pot_note: For soil growing, use a moist but well-drained mix and a pot with drainage holes. It can also be grown in chlorine-free water; if grown in water, the soil-mix calculator does not apply and the water should be changed weekly.

watering.rule: In soil, keep the mix moist but not saturated. In water culture, use chlorine-free water and change it weekly.

by_season.summer: For soil-grown plants, check moisture more often and keep the mix lightly moist without waterlogging; for water-grown plants, refresh the water weekly.
by_season.monsoon: Check soil-grown pots before watering and make sure excess water drains; continue the weekly water change for water-grown plants.
by_season.autumn: Keep soil lightly moist according to drying; in water culture, continue weekly water changes.
by_season.winter: Check the soil before watering and protect from cold drafts; continue weekly water changes if grown in water.

watering.avoid: Avoid waterlogged potting mix, prolonged harsh direct sunlight, and stagnant water.

common_mistakes: Confusing the plant with true bamboo
Allowing soil to remain waterlogged
Leaving water culture unchanged for long periods
Exposing the plant to harsh direct sun

name: Rubber Plant
light: Bright indirect light or partial shade; protect it from harsh afternoon sun and cold drafts.
pot_note: Use a soil-based, well-drained potting mix and a stable pot with drainage holes. Keep it in a consistent position and wipe dust from leaves with a soft damp cloth.

watering.rule: Water regularly during active growth but avoid overwatering. Let excess water drain and reduce watering when growth slows in cooler months.

by_season.summer: Check the surface regularly and water when needed; do not allow the pot to remain saturated.
by_season.monsoon: Check moisture before watering and empty the saucer; humid conditions can slow drying.
by_season.autumn: Begin adjusting watering as growth slows, checking the soil before each watering.
by_season.winter: Water less often during slower growth; do not water again while the mix is still wet.

watering.avoid: Avoid overwatering, cold drafts, sudden temperature changes, and constantly moving the plant.

common_mistakes: Overwatering
Placing it in cold drafts
Moving it frequently
Allowing dust to accumulate on leaves
